title: Bound a lookup cache by recent use

blocks.text: The edge service caches geo-IP answers by address so it doesn't call the lookup provider for every request. Memory allows a fixed number of answers. When a new one arrives and the cache is full, the answer that has gone longest without being *used* must go: an address read a second ago stays, even if it was first cached long before the others. Answers arrive one at a time, and at start-up a warm-up job loads the previous run's answers in one `putAll`; the bound must hold either way.

`RecentLookups.java` extends `LinkedHashMap`, and its constructor already passes `orderedByUse()` as the third argument of `LinkedHashMap(int, float, boolean)` (see that constructor's javadoc). Finish the three `TODO` methods, about four lines in total:

items: `orderedByUse()`: the order that makes "the eldest entry" the least recently used one;
`removeEldestEntry`: keeps the cache at no more than `capacity` answers;
`nextToDrop()`: the address that would be dropped next, or `null` when the cache is empty.

cases.says: the cache stores, overwrites and answers lookups like any map, and has nothing to drop when empty
answers added one at a time never take the cache past its capacity, and the newest one stays
a warm-up batch larger than the capacity leaves exactly the capacity, the latest answers of the batch
an answer that was read after it was added is kept over an older answer nobody read
a cache filled to its capacity keeps every answer

origin.section: Extend a Class Through the Hook It Documents: LinkedHashMap Calls removeEldestEntry from put and putAll

concepts: A class designed for extension offers a protected hook whose callers its javadoc names; LinkedHashMap's removeEldestEntry is called from put and putAll, while an override of put is skipped by putAll.
